You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"partly_recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"A utility voltage sag occurred and chillers failed to restart, indicating mechanical cooling may be compromised; the rule directs verifying cooling and planning for thermal buffer depletion.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]},{"rule_id":"R-010","because":"A utility voltage sag tripped multiple chillers offline and manual restarts are required across two data halls; the rule mandates a load-based restart sequence across data halls.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S81","AZ-AUE-2023:S82"]},{"rule_id":"R-012","because":"Chillers supporting the data halls have tripped offline; the rule requires confirming the minimum operational chiller count per data hall.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S19","AZ-AUE-2023:S20","AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]},{"rule_id":"R-014","because":"Multiple chillers require manual restart and the Chiller Management System has not been changed to prevent restart failures; the rule advises staging extra technicians.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S81","AZ-AUE-2023:S82"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running and assess thermal buffer status.","rule_id":"R-001"},{"action":"Count how many chillers each impacted data hall still has running against its minimum requirement (at least four per hall).","rule_id":"R-012"},{"action":"Sequence manual chiller restarts by data hall load so that every impacted data hall gets partial cooling early, rather than finishing one data hall before starting the next.","rule_id":"R-010"},{"action":"Increase technician staffing at the datacenter so manual restart procedures can be executed promptly and in parallel across data halls.","rule_id":"R-014"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","reason":"Mechanical cooling is confirmed shut down (chillers failed to restart) and multiple chillers require manual restart across more than one data hall, triggering escalation conditions for R-001, R-010, and R-012."},"not_covered":["No rule addresses the specific scenario of a voltage sag causing 13 chillers to fail automatic restart while the site is not on generator power and storms are not mentioned.","No rule covers the coordination of remote resets versus manual restarts when chillers fail to restart automatically after a voltage sag.","No rule addresses the potential need to transfer the datacenter to generator power when only a voltage sag (not a full outage) has occurred and storms are not active."]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"The voltage sag caused cooling system chillers for multiple datacenters to shut down."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Incremental load increases over time in the Availability Zone resulted in a chiller operating configuration that was susceptible to a timing defect in the Chiller Management System."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"By the time the team reached the final five chillers requiring a manual restart, the water inside the pump system for these chillers (chilled water loop) had reached temperatures that were too high to allow them to be restarted."},{"id":"F4","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"In this scenario, the restart is inhibited by a self-protection mechanism that acts to prevent damage to the chiller that would occur by processing water at the elevated temperatures."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"At 11:34 UTC, as temperatures continued to increase, our onsite datacenter team began a remote shutdown of remaining networking, compute, and storage infrastructure in the impacted data halls to protect data durability, infrastructure health, and address the thermal runaway."},{"id":"F6","kind":"response","text":"This shutdown allowed the chilled water loop to return to a safe temperature which allowed us to restart the chillers."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We have de-risked this failure to restart due to voltage fluctuations, by implementing a change to the control timing logic on the Chiller Management System (Completed)."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"Emergency Operation Procedure for manual restarts of simultaneous chiller failures has changed from an ‘adjacent’ sequence to a data hall ‘load based’ sequence to ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling, to slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored (Completed)."},{"id":"F9","kind":"remediation","text":"Following this incident, as a temporary mitigation, we increased technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of our chillers prior to the change to the Chiller Management System to prevent restart failures."},{"id":"F10","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Based on our incident analysis the staffing levels at the time would have been sufficient to prevent impact if a ‘load based' chiller restart sequence had been followed, which we have since implemented (Completed)."},{"id":"F11","kind":"impact","text":"At 10:30 UTC some networking, compute, and storage infrastructure began to shutdown automatically as data hall temperatures increased, impacting service availability."}]}
